title: Large-area two-dimensional MoO3 as a high-κ dielectric for van der Waals integration
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75196-1

The large-scale integration of high-κ dielectric materials with 2D semiconductors is important for the miniaturization of 2D electronics. Here, the authors report the growth of millimeter-scale high-κ MoO3 crystalline films and their application as gate dielectric for 2D transistors and complementary logic devices.

title: Allelic variation of an LRR only protein confers dual pathogen resistance in Arabidopsis
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75012-w

Plant LRR proteins perceive diverse pathogen-derived signals. Here the authors show that allelic variations in an Arabidopsis LRIP1 underlies dual functions in combating distinct pathogens and link local climate adaptation with pathogen-specific immune signaling.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of scattering exceptional points
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75187-2

Exceptional points govern unique wave scattering, yet their topology is often hidden in steady states. Here, the authors map these static singularities to dynamic wave packets, revealing how their topological charge is imprinted onto spatiotemporal vortices using liquid surface waves.

title: Hydrogen bond network disruption enables efficient direct reactive capture of CO<sub>2</sub> from flue gas
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74647-z

Electrochemical CO2 conversion from flue gas is hindered by low CO2 concentration and competing oxygen reduction. Here, the authors report the control over hydrogen-bond donation in binary organic electrolytes for selective CO production from O2-containing streams and suppressed side reactions.

title: Learning regularities in noise engages both neural predictive activity and representational changes
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74824-0

Extracting regularities from a noisy environment is fundamental to cognition, yet the underlying neural mechanisms remain unclear. Here, the authors use MEG and MVPA to reveal two temporally dissociable mechanisms: rapid predictive activity, followed by slower representational change.

title: Causal effects of wildfire PM<sub>2.5</sub> on hospital costs and length of stay in Brazil
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75157-8

This study links 184.5 million hospitalizations in Brazil to wildfire-specific PM₂.₅, using wind-driven variation within a causal framework. It finds higher hospitalization costs and longer stays for all-cause, respiratory, and cardiovascular diseases, with stronger effects in children.

title: Thermodynamically programmed one-pot CRISPR platform for point-of-care SNP genotyping
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75358-1

One-pot CRISPR diagnostics are limited by kinetic conflict between isothermal amplification and CRISPR detection. By thermodynamically programming reaction order into DNA primers, the authors create staged amplification enabling rapid, sensitive, single-step nucleic acid testing.

title: Magnonic spontaneous oscillation induced by parametric pumping
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-71916-9

Parametric pumping in a YIG thin film generates ultrasharp spontaneous spin-wave modes that behave as auto-oscillators with quality factors exceeding 200,000 and can phase-lock to an external stimulus.
